key_insight: 3D human motion and 2D video generation are mutually beneficial and should be generated together: 3D motions provide structural priors for realism/consistency, while video models supply rich visual generalization for plausible motion.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between standalone motion synthesis and video generation by synchronously producing coherent 3D poses and realistic 2D videos, reducing mismatches between motion structure and visual appearance.
method: Co-generation framework that couples two video diffusion models (one focused on 3D motion representations, one on 2D video frames) to generate motions and videos jointly.
Cross-conditioning / mutual guidance between the two VDMs (shared latents or iterative bidirectional conditioning) to enforce temporal and structural consistency.
Training objectives include motion–video consistency loss and temporal coherence, leveraging pre-trained video models to improve motion generalization.
impact: Enables generation of visually coherent videos with physically plausible 3D motion, simplifying pipelines for animation, virtual humans, and data synthesis; useful for researchers and engineers working on multi-modal generative models and downstream animation tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two coupled diffusion models (3D motion VDM ↔ 2D video VDM) with bidirectional arrows for mutual conditioning
Before/after examples: separate motion vs. co-generated motion+video frames to illustrate improved realism and alignment
Loss schematic showing consistency loss between 3D poses and rendered 2D frames and temporal coherence
Timeline visualization of synchronized 3D pose sequences alongside corresponding video frames
paper_title: CoMoVi: Co-Generation of 3D Human Motions and Realistic Videos
paper_authors: Chengfeng Zhao, Jiazhi Shu, Yubo Zhao, Tianyu Huang, Jiahao Lu
